result.title: Which Answers Agree? Evaluating Self-Consistency from Incomplete Logs
result.summary: Self-consistency answers a question by generating multiple responses and selecting the most frequent answer. Its evaluation requires both correctness labels and information about which responses agree; correctness labels alone generally determine neither voting accuracy nor the benefit of additional votes. For tasks in which all correct responses map to the same normalized answer, we derive sharp accuracy bounds using classical stochastic majorization, refined by abstention counts and answer-category limits. We also derive sharp bounds on accuracy changes across voting budgets that share a response pool. When answer-category counts are available, we introduce Plurality-U, a count-based dynamic program that exactly averages voting accuracy over all fixed-size subsets, eliminating finite-pool Monte Carlo error. On 1,403,520 stored outputs from recent reasoning models in Scorio Lite and Scorio Trace, recording abstention counts and answer options cuts the width of SuperGPQA accuracy intervals by more than half. For moving from 9 to 17 votes, our bounds reduce interval width by a median of 77.7% on SuperGPQA and 72.3% on 14 GPQA and Adaptive-Consistency pools, compared with a baseline that combines separate accuracy bounds. Exact computation has lower paired median runtime than 2,000-subset Monte Carlo in 14 of 15 tested pool-budget settings. These results clarify what incomplete logs can establish and provide an exact evaluation procedure when answer counts are retained.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究在日志不完整（只记录正确性标签而缺少「哪些回答一致」信息）时如何评价 self-consistency 投票准确率：用随机 majorization 推导准确率上界，并借弃答计数与答案类别数收紧区间，还提出 Plurality-U 动态规划以精确计算固定规模子集上的平均投票准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其计数式的投票收益与预算扩展分析，或可迁移到 LVR 中多个 latent 假设／并行采样聚合的评估，弃答计数也与 STOP 决策的收益成本核算相近；但论文只面向纯文本推理基准，未涉及视觉状态或 latent 内容，迁移适用性需核查。
